Having heard learned counsel for the parties, particularly taking into consideration the conduct of the petitioner of sending obscene video of victim to her husband, I am not inclined to grant bail to the petitioner.
Hence, the instant bail application is dismissed.
However, as the petitioner was arrested on 16.04.2019, it is expected that the trial court shall expedite the trial."
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner is in judicial custody since 16.04.2019.
The statements of material prosecution witnesses including victim 'S' (PW-01) and the complainant (PW-03) have already been recorded before the competent criminal Court.

Learned counsel submitted that since the statements of the material prosecution witnesses have already been recorded before the competent criminal Court, the further incarceration of the petitioner is not warranted.
There is nothing on record to indicate that delay in trial is attributable to the petitioner.

Learned counsel further submitted that there are no factors at play in the case at hand that may work against grant of bail to the petitioner.
[2024:RJ-JD:50547] (3 of 5) [CRLMB-13150/2024]
4.
On the contrary to the submissions of learned counsel for the petitioner, learned counsel for the complainant submitted that this is fourth bail application and there is no change in circumstances.

Learned counsel submitted that orders dated 23.10.2019, 19.01.2021 and 19.12.2023 passed by the co-ordinate Benches of this Court clearly indicate that after taking into consideration the facts and circumstances of the case, it was deemed proper by the Co-ordinate Benches not to grant the benefit of bail to the petitioner.
It was thus prayed that the present bail application may be dismissed.
5. Heard learned counsel for the parties.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is a well settled principle of law that when the successive bail application comes before the Court, the Court should be very conscious while considering the successive bail application.

7. The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of 'State of Maharashtra vs. Captain Buddhikota Subharao' reported in AIR 1989 SC 2292 was pleased to hold that successive bail application can be entertained by the Court when substantial change is established by the accused, which would entitle him for granting bail in successive bail application.

entities.text: State of Maharashtra vs. Captain Buddhikota Subharao' reported in AIR 1989 SC 2292
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Court should not pass the order of releasing him on bail in successive bail application merely establishing some cosmetic change between time gap of two applications.

There should be drastic change during the period between two applications,
which would entitle the accused for bail.
(Emphasis supplied)

8. In the case of 'Kalyan Chandra Sarkar vs. Rajesh Ranjan @ Pappu Yadav' reported in AIR 2005 SC 921, the Hon'ble Apex [2024:RJ-JD:50547] (4 of 5) [CRLMB-13150/2024] Court has held that the Court before entertaining such successive bail applications must consider the reasons and grounds on which the earlier bail applications were rejected.

entities.text: Kalyan Chandra Sarkar vs. Rajesh Ranjan @ Pappu Yadav' reported in AIR 2005 SC 921
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: When a successive bail application comes before the Court, it is the duty of the Court to record that what are the fresh grounds which persuaded to take a view different from the one taken in the earlier application.

9. Recently, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of 'X. vs. State of Rajasthan & Anr':
Special Leave Petition (Crl. No.13378/2024) in para 15 and 16 pleased to observe as under:-
"15.

entities.text: X. vs. State of Rajasthan & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Over a period of time, we have noticed two things i.e., (I) either bail is granted after the charge is framed and just before the victim is to be examined by the prosecution before the trial court, or (ii) bail is granted once the recording of the oral evidence of the victim is complete by looking into some discrepancies here or there in the deposition and thereby testing the credibility of the victim.
16.
We are of the view that the aforesaid is not a correct practice that the Courts below should adopt.
Once the trial commences, it should be allowed to reach to its final conclusion which may either result in the conviction of the accused or acquittal of the accused.

The moment the High Court exercises its discretion in favour of the accused and orders release of the accused on bail by looking into the deposition of the victim, it will have its own impact on the pending trial when it comes to appreciating the oral evidence of the victim.

It is only in the event if the trial gets unduly delayed and that too for not fault on the part of the accused, the Court may be justified in ordering his release on bail on the ground that right of the accused to have a speedy trial has been infringed."
10.
This Court, on a careful perusal of the case file, do not find any change in circumstance warranting fresh application of mind on the grounds raised by the petitioner in the present bail application.
In the opinion of this Court, enlarging the petitioner on bail, when the trial against him has progressed substantively, would impede the progress of trial.

Hence, this Court is not inclined to Upendra Singh @ Vipin Singh vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:50547) on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127022287/
